<p style="text-align:center;margin-bottom:0pt;margin-top:0pt;text-indent:0%;font-weight:bold;font-size:10pt;font-family:Times New Roman;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">(Unaudited) </p>
<p style="margin-bottom:0pt;margin-top:0pt;text-indent:0%;font-size:12pt;font-family:Times New Roman;">&#160;</p><ix:nonNumeric id="F_000431" name="us-gaap:OrganizationConsolidationAndPresentationOfFinancialStatementsDisclosureTextBlock" contextRef="C_0000087347_20210101_20210930" escape="true">
<p style="margin-bottom:0pt;margin-top:0pt;text-indent:0%;font-weight:bold;font-size:10pt;font-family:Times New Roman;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">1.&#160;&#160; <span style="text-decoration:underline;">Basis of Presentation</span> </p>
<p style="text-align:justify;margin-bottom:0pt;margin-top:6pt;text-indent:0%;font-size:10pt;font-family:Times New Roman;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">The accompanying unaudited consolidated financial statements of Schlumberger Limited and its subsidiaries (&#8220;Schlumberger&#8221;) have been prepared in accordance with generally accepted accounting principles in the United States of America for interim financial information and with the instructions to Form 10-Q and Article 10 of Regulation S-X.&#160;&#160;Accordingly, they do not include all of the information and footnotes required by generally accepted accounting principles for complete financial statements.&#160;&#160;In the opinion of Schlumberger management, all adjustments considered necessary for a fair statement have been included in the accompanying unaudited financial statements.&#160;&#160;All intercompany transactions and balances have been eliminated in consolidation.&#160;&#160;Operating results for the nine-month period ended September 30, 2021 are not necessarily indicative of the results that may be expected for the full year ending December&#160;31, 2021.&#160;&#160;The December&#160;31, 2020 balance sheet information has been derived from the Schlumberger 2020 audited financial statements.&#160;&#160;For further information, refer to the <span style="font-style:italic;">Consolidated Financial Statements</span> and notes thereto included in the Schlumberger Annual Report on Form 10-K for the year ended December&#160;31, 2020, filed with the Securities and Exchange Commission on January&#160;27, 2021. </p></ix:nonNumeric><ix:nonNumeric id="F_000432" name="us-gaap:RestructuringAndRelatedActivitiesDisclosureTextBlock" contextRef="C_0000087347_20210101_20210930" escape="true" continuedAt="F_000432_dcnt_771382ea-df68-458c-8453-9a7de64a1b13">
<p style="text-align:justify;margin-top:18pt;margin-bottom:0pt;text-indent:0%;font-weight:bold;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">2.&#160;&#160; <span style="text-decoration:underline;">Charges and Credits</span></p>

<p style="text-align:justify;margin-bottom:0pt;margin-top:0pt;margin-left:6.67%;text-indent:0%;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;">&#160;</p>
<p style="text-align:justify;margin-top:0pt;margin-bottom:0pt;text-indent:0%;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;">&#160;</p></ix:nonNumeric>
<p style="text-align:center;margin-top:12pt;margin-bottom:0pt;text-indent:0%;font-size:10pt;font-family:Times New Roman;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">9</p>
<hr style="page-break-after:always" />
<p style="margin-bottom:0pt;margin-top:0pt;text-indent:0%;font-size:12pt;font-family:Times New Roman;">&#160;</p><ix:continuation id="F_000432_dcnt_771382ea-df68-458c-8453-9a7de64a1b13" continuedAt="F_000432_dcnt_235cf8ab-f8f9-4752-801f-414bd10d815c">
<p style="margin-bottom:0pt;margin-top:0pt;text-indent:0%;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;">&#160;</p>
<p style="text-align:justify;margin-bottom:0pt;margin-top:0pt;text-indent:0%;font-style:italic;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-weight:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">First quarter 2020:</p>
<p style="text-align:justify;margin-top:0pt;margin-bottom:0pt;text-indent:0%;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;">&#160;</p>
<div style="align:left;">
<table border="0" cellspacing="0" cellpadding="0" style="border-collapse:collapse; width:100%;">
<tr>
<td valign="top" style="width:3.33%;white-space:nowrap">
<p style="text-align:justify;margin-bottom:0pt;margin-top:0pt;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;color:#auto;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;letter-spacing:0pt;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;">&#160;</p></td>
<td valign="top" style="width:3.33%;white-space:nowrap">
<p style="text-align:justify;margin-bottom:0pt;margin-top:0pt;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;color:#auto;font-size:10pt;font-family:'Times New Roman';text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;letter-spacing:0pt;"><span style="font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-decoration:none;Background-color:#auto;color:#auto;font-size:10pt;font-family:'Times New Roman';text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;letter-spacing:0pt;"></span><span style="font-size:10pt;font-family:'Times New Roman'">&#8226;</span></p></td>
<td valign="top">
<p style="text-align:justify;margin-bottom:0pt;margin-top:0pt;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;color:#auto;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;letter-spacing:0pt;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;"><span style="Background-color:#auto;text-decoration:none;"></span><span style="color:#000000;">Geopolitical events that increased the supply of low-priced oil to the global market occurred at the same time that demand weakened due to the worldwide effects of the COVID-19 pandemic, leading to a collapse in oil prices during March 2020.&#160;&#160;As a result, Schlumberger&#8217;s market capitalization deteriorated significantly compared to the end of 2019.&#160;&#160;Schlumberger&#8217;s stock price reached a low during the first quarter of 2020 not seen since 1995.&#160;&#160;Additionally, the Philadelphia Oil Services Sector index, which is comprised of companies involved in the oil services sector, reached an all-time low.&#160;&#160;As a result of these facts, Schlumberger determined that it was more likely than not that the fair value of certain of its reporting units were less than their carrying value.&#160;&#160;Therefore, Schlumberger performed an interim goodwill impairment test that resulted in a $<ix:nonFraction unitRef="U_iso4217USD" id="F_000519" name="us-gaap:GoodwillAndIntangibleAssetImpairment" contextRef="C_0000087347_20200101_20200331" decimals="-8" scale="9">3.1</ix:nonFraction> billion goodwill impairment charge.</span></p></td></tr></table></div>
<p style="text-align:justify;margin-top:12pt;margin-bottom:0pt;margin-left:6.67%;text-indent:0%;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">Schlumberger used the income approach to estimate the fair value of its reporting units, but also considered the market approach to validate the results.&#160;&#160;The income approach estimates the fair value by discounting each reporting unit&#8217;s estimated future cash flows using Schlumberger&#8217;s estimate of the discount rate, or expected return, that a marketplace participant would have required as of the valuation date.&#160;&#160;The market approach includes the use of comparative multiples to corroborate the discounted cash flow results. The market approach involves significant judgement involved in the selection of the appropriate peer group companies and valuation multiples.</p>
<p style="text-align:justify;margin-bottom:0pt;margin-top:0pt;margin-left:6.67%;text-indent:0%;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;">&#160;</p>
<p style="text-align:justify;margin-top:2pt;margin-bottom:0pt;margin-left:6.67%;text-indent:0%;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">Some of the more significant assumptions inherent in the income approach include the estimated future net annual cash flows for each reporting unit and the discount rate.&#160;&#160;Schlumberger selected the assumptions used in the discounted cash flow projections using historical data supplemented by current and anticipated market conditions and estimated growth rates.&#160;&#160;Schlumberger&#8217;s estimates are based upon assumptions believed to be reasonable.&#160;&#160;However, given the inherent uncertainty in determining the assumptions underlying a discounted cash flow analysis, particularly in the current volatile market, actual results may differ from those used in Schlumberger&#8217;s valuations which could result in additional impairment charges in the future.</p>
<p style="text-align:justify;margin-bottom:0pt;margin-top:0pt;margin-left:6.67%;text-indent:0%;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;">&#160;</p>
<p style="text-align:justify;margin-top:2pt;margin-bottom:0pt;margin-left:6.67%;text-indent:0%;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">The discount rates utilized to value Schlumberger&#8217;s reporting units were between <ix:nonFraction unitRef="U_xbrlipure" id="F_000520" name="slb:DiscountRateUtilized" contextRef="C_0000087347_srtRangeAxis_srtMinimumMember_20200101_20200331" decimals="3" scale="-2">12.0</ix:nonFraction>% and <ix:nonFraction unitRef="U_xbrlipure" id="F_000521" name="slb:DiscountRateUtilized" contextRef="C_0000087347_srtRangeAxis_srtMaximumMember_20200101_20200331" decimals="3" scale="-2">13.5</ix:nonFraction>%, depending on the risks and uncertainty inherent in the respective reporting unit as well as the size of the reporting unit.&#160;&#160;Assuming all other assumptions and inputs used in each of the respective discounted cash flow analysis were held constant, a <ix:nonFraction unitRef="U_xbrlipure" id="F_000522" name="slb:ExpectedIncreaseDecreaseInDiscountRateAssumption" contextRef="C_0000087347_20200101_20200331" decimals="4" scale="-4">50</ix:nonFraction>-basis point increase or decrease in the discount rate assumptions would have changed the fair value of the <ix:nonFraction unitRef="U_slbUnit" id="F_000523" name="slb:NumberOfReportingUnitsFairValueToBeImpacted" contextRef="C_0000087347_20200101_20200331" decimals="INF" format="ixt-sec:numwordsen">seven</ix:nonFraction> reporting units, on average, by less than <ix:nonFraction unitRef="U_xbrlipure" id="F_000524" name="slb:ExpectedPercentageChangeInFairValueOfReportingUnits" contextRef="C_0000087347_srtRangeAxis_srtMaximumMember_20200101_20200331" decimals="2" scale="-2">5</ix:nonFraction>%.</p>
<p style="text-align:justify;margin-bottom:0pt;margin-top:0pt;margin-left:6.67%;text-indent:0%;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;">&#160;</p>
<div style="align:left;">

<p style="text-align:justify;margin-bottom:0pt;margin-top:18pt;text-indent:0%;font-weight:bold;font-size:10pt;font-family:Times New Roman;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">8.&#160;&#160; <span style="text-decoration:underline;">Derivative Instruments and Hedging Activities</span> </p>
<p style="text-align:justify;margin-bottom:0pt;margin-top:6pt;text-indent:0%;font-size:10pt;font-family:Times New Roman;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">As a multinational company, Schlumberger conducts its business in over <ix:nonFraction unitRef="U_slbCountry" id="F_000809" name="us-gaap:NumberOfCountriesInWhichEntityOperates" contextRef="C_0000087347_20210930" decimals="INF">120</ix:nonFraction> countries.&#160;&#160;Schlumberger&#8217;s functional currency is primarily the US dollar.&#160;&#160;</p>
<p style="text-align:justify;margin-bottom:0pt;margin-top:12pt;text-indent:0%;font-size:10pt;font-family:Times New Roman;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">Schlumberger is exposed to risks on future cash flows to the extent that the local currency is not the functional currency and expenses denominated in local currency are not equal to revenues denominated in local currency.&#160;&#160;Schlumberger uses foreign currency forward contracts to provide a hedge against a portion of these cash flow risks.&#160; These contracts are accounted for as cash flow hedges, with the changes in the fair value of the hedge recorded on the <span style="font-style:italic;">Consolidated Balance Sheet </span>and in <span style="font-style:italic;">Accumulated Other Comprehensive Loss.&#160; </span>Amounts recorded in<span style="font-style:italic;"> Accumulated Other Comprehensive Loss </span>are reclassified into earnings in the same period or periods that the hedged item is recognized in earnings.&#160; </p>

normal;">Schlumberger is also exposed to risks on future cash flows relating to certain of its fixed rate debt denominated in currencies other than the functional currency.&#160;&#160;Schlumberger <p style="text-align:justify;margin-top:2pt;margin-bottom:0pt;text-indent:0%;color:#000000;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">Due to the actions taken by Schlumberger to reduce its global workforce during 2020, Schlumberger experienced a significant reduction in the expected aggregate years of future service of its employees in its US postretirement medical plan. Accordingly, Schlumberger recorded a curtailment gain of $<ix:nonFraction unitRef="U_iso4217USD" id="F_001128" name="us-gaap:DefinedBenefitPlanRecognizedNetGainLossDueToSettlementsAndCurtailments1" contextRef="C_0000087347_us-gaapRetirementPlanTypeAxis_us-gaapDefinedBenefitPostretirementHealthCoverageMember_20200401_20200630" decimals="-6" scale="6">69</ix:nonFraction> million during the second quarter of 2020 relating to this plan. The curtailment gain includes recognition of the decrease in the benefit obligation as well as a portion of the previously unrecognized prior service credit, reflecting the reduction in expected years of future service.&#160; As a result of the curtailment, Schlumberger performed a remeasurement of the plan, which had an immaterial impact.&#160; This gain was classified in <span style="font-style:italic;">Impairments &#38; other</span> in the <span style="font-style:italic;">Consolidated Statement of Income (Loss)</span>.&#160; See Note 2 &#8211; <span style="font-style:italic;">Charges and Credits</span>.</p></ix:nonNumeric>

<p style="text-align:justify;margin-top:6pt;margin-bottom:0pt;text-indent:0%;color:#000000;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">Third-quarter revenue grew 4% sequentially led by Well Construction and Reservoir Performance.&#160;&#160;The revenue growth in these Divisions more than offset the impact of transitory global supply and logistics constraints in Production Systems. </p>
<p style="text-align:justify;margin-top:12pt;margin-bottom:0pt;text-indent:0%;color:#000000;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">Geographically, international revenue of $4.68 billion grew 4% sequentially and 11% year-on-year and is on track to meet our double-digit revenue growth ambition for the second half of 2021 compared to the same period last year.&#160;&#160;The international sequential revenue increase was led by double-digit growth in Latin America complemented by sustained activity in the Europe/CIS/Africa and Middle East &#38; Asia areas. In North America, revenue of $1.13 billion grew 4% sequentially mainly driven by a strong seasonal rebound in land drilling, higher Asset Performance Solutions (&#8220;APS&#8221;) revenue in Canada, and an increase in drilling revenue in North America offshore.</p>
<p style="text-align:justify;margin-top:12pt;margin-bottom:0pt;text-indent:0%;color:#000000;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">Among the Divisions, Well Construction continued its growth momentum, with revenue increasing 8% sequentially due to higher international and North America drilling activity both on land and offshore. Similarly, Reservoir Performance revenue increased 7% sequentially from higher exploration and appraisal activity across the international markets. Revenue from Digital &#38; Integration and Production Systems was essentially flat.</p>
<p style="text-align:justify;margin-top:12pt;margin-bottom:0pt;text-indent:0%;color:#000000;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">Sequentially, third-quarter pretax segment operating margin expanded by 120 basis points (&#8220;bps&#8221;) to 16%, representing its highest level since 2015 and a fifth consecutive quarter of margin expansion.&#160;&#160;This growth was driven by the Well Construction and Reservoir Performance Divisions. </p>
<p style="text-align:justify;margin-top:12pt;margin-bottom:0pt;text-indent:0%;color:#000000;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">Looking ahead, the fourth quarter of 2021 is anticipated to be another quarter of growth, and Schlumberger expects to close 2021 with strong momentum that will set the foundation for an exceptional growth cycle.</p>
<p style="text-align:center;margin-top:12pt;margin-bottom:0pt;text-indent:0%;font-size:10pt;font-family:Times New Roman;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">20</p>
<hr style="page-break-after:always" />
<p style="margin-bottom:0pt;margin-top:0pt;text-indent:0%;font-size:12pt;font-family:Times New Roman;">&#160;</p>
<p style="text-align:justify;margin-top:12pt;margin-bottom:0pt;text-indent:0%;color:#000000;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;"><span style="color:#000000;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">The industry macro fundamentals have visibly strengthened this year, particularly in recent weeks&#8212;with demand recovery, oil and gas commodity prices at recent highs, low inventory levels, and encouraging trends in pandemic containment efforts. </span><span style="color:#000000;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">Absent a recession or pandemic-related setback, t</span><span style="color:#000000;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">hese</span><span style="color:#000000;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;"> favorable conditions are expected to materially drive investment over the next few years&#8212; particularly internationally&#8212;and result in exceptional multiyear capital spending growth globally, both on land and offshore. </span></p>
<p style="text-align:justify;margin-top:18pt;margin-bottom:0pt;text-indent:0%;font-weight:bold;font-size:10pt;font-family:Times New Roman;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">Digital &#38; Integration</p>
<p style="text-align:justify;margin-top:6pt;margin-bottom:0pt;text-indent:0%;color:#000000;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">Digital &#38; Integration revenue of $812 million declined 1% sequentially<span style="color:#FF0000;"> </span>as higher APS project revenue was offset by lower digital solutions revenue following strong software sales in the second quarter. Revenue grew in North America, Latin America, and Middle East &#38; Asia, offset by lower revenue in Europe/CIS/Africa.</p>
<p style="text-align:justify;margin-top:12pt;margin-bottom:0pt;text-indent:0%;color:#000000;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">Digital &#38; Integration pretax operating margin of 35% expanded 154 bps sequentially, primarily due to increased profitability from APS projects.</p>
<p style="text-align:justify;margin-top:18pt;margin-bottom:0pt;text-indent:0%;font-weight:bold;font-size:10pt;font-family:Times New Roman;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">Reservoir Performance</p>
<p style="text-align:justify;margin-top:6pt;margin-bottom:0pt;text-indent:0%;color:#000000;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">Reservoir Performance revenue of $1.19 billion increased 7% sequentially due to higher exploration and appraisal programs across the international markets. </p>
<p style="text-align:justify;margin-top:12pt;margin-bottom:0pt;text-indent:0%;color:#000000;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">Reservoir Performance pretax operating margin of 16% expanded 202 bps sequentially. Profitability was boosted by higher offshore and exploration activity and a favorable technology mix, particularly in Latin America and Africa.</p>
<p style="text-align:justify;margin-top:18pt;margin-bottom:0pt;text-indent:0%;font-weight:bold;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">Well Construction</p>
<p style="text-align:justify;margin-top:6pt;margin-bottom:0pt;text-indent:0%;color:#000000;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">Well Construction revenue of $2.27 billion increased 8% sequentially due to higher land and offshore drilling across the international markets and increased rig activity in North America. North America revenue growth was driven by strong seasonal rebound on land drilling in Canada and higher offshore drilling in the Gulf of Mexico, notwithstanding the hurricane effects during the quarter. International revenue was driven by double-digit growth in Latin America, Africa, and Russia &#38; Central Asia from the combination of increased offshore exploration activity and the peak of summer land drilling campaigns.</p>
<p style="text-align:justify;margin-top:12pt;margin-bottom:0pt;text-indent:0%;color:#000000;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">Well Construction pretax operating margin of 15% improved sequentially by 230 bps due to higher drilling revenue, boosted by the favorable mix of activity and new technology.</p>
<p style="text-align:justify;margin-top:18pt;margin-bottom:0pt;text-indent:0%;font-weight:bold;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">Production Systems</p>
<p style="text-align:justify;margin-top:6pt;margin-bottom:0pt;text-indent:0%;color:#000000;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">Production Systems revenue of $1.67 billion was essentially flat sequentially, as revenue increases in subsea and well production systems were offset by a revenue decline in midstream production systems. Revenue was partially impacted by transitory global supply and logistics constraints.</p>
<p style="text-align:justify;margin-top:12pt;margin-bottom:0pt;text-indent:0%;color:#000000;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">Production Systems pretax operating margin of 10% was essentially flat sequentially.</p>
<p style="text-align:justify;margin-top:18pt;margin-bottom:0pt;text-indent:0%;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;">&#160;</p>
<p style="text-align:justify;margin-top:18pt;margin-bottom:0pt;text-indent:0%;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;">&#160;</p>
<p style="text-align:justify;margin-top:18pt;margin-bottom:0pt;text-indent:0%;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;">&#160;</p>
<p style="text-align:justify;margin-bottom:0pt;margin-top:0pt;text-indent:0%;font-weight:bold;;font-size:5pt;">&#160;</p>
<p style="text-align:justify;margin-bottom:0pt;margin-top:0pt;text-indent:0%;font-weight:bold;;font-size:5pt;">&#160;</p>
<p style="text-align:justify;margin-bottom:0pt;margin-top:2pt;margin-left:3.33%;text-indent:-3.33%;font-size:9pt;">&#160;</p>
<p style="text-align:justify;margin-bottom:0pt;margin-top:0pt;text-indent:0%;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;">&#160;</p>
<p style="text-align:center;margin-top:12pt;margin-bottom:0pt;text-indent:0%;font-size:10pt;font-family:Times New Roman;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">21</p>
<hr style="page-break-after:always" />

<p style="text-align:justify;margin-bottom:0pt;margin-top:6pt;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:9pt;">Charges and credits are described in detail in Note 2 to the <span style="font-style:italic;">Consolidated Financial Statements.</span></p></td></tr></table></div>
<p style="text-align:justify;margin-bottom:0pt;margin-top:0pt;text-indent:0%;font-size:10pt;">&#160;</p>
<p style="text-align:justify;margin-bottom:0pt;margin-top:0pt;text-indent:0%;color:#000000;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">Nine-month 2021 revenue of $16.7 billion decreased 8% year-on-year. Revenue declined particularly in North America, following the divestitures of the<span style="font-family:AECKA F+ Univers;"> </span>OneStim<sup style="font-size:85%;line-height:120%;vertical-align:top">&#174;</sup> pressure pumping business and the low-flow artificial lift business during the fourth quarter 2020. These divestitures<span style="font-family:AECKA F+ Univers;"> </span>were consistent with Schlumberger&#8217;s strategy to focus on high-grading and rationalizing its business portfolio to expand margins,<span style="font-family:AECKA F+ Univers;"> </span>minimize earnings volatility, and focus on more capital efficient businesses. Excluding the impact of these divestitures, which<span style="font-family:AECKA F+ Univers;"> </span>generated $1.1 billion of revenue (all of which was in North America) during the first nine months of 2020, global revenue declined 2% year-on-year, reflecting the significant fall in activity following the historic demand destruction driven by the COVID-19 pandemic that commenced in early 2020.&#160;&#160;</p>
<p style="text-align:justify;margin-top:12pt;margin-bottom:0pt;text-indent:0%;color:#000000;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">In North America revenue declined 26% year-on-year&#59; however, excluding the impact of the previously described divestitures, nine-month revenue only declined 2%.&#160;&#160;International revenue also declined 2% driven by significant activity decreases in Europe/CIS/Africa and the Middle East &#38; Asia, partially offset by an increase in revenue in Latin America.</p>
<p style="text-align:justify;margin-top:12pt;margin-bottom:0pt;text-indent:0%;color:#000000;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">Nine-month 2021 pretax operating margin of 14% was 458 bps higher compared to the same period last year despite the 8% decline in revenue, due to the divestiture of certain businesses in North America, which were previously dilutive to margins, combined with reduced depreciation and amortization expense following the asset impairment charges recorded during 2020 and the effects of cost reduction measures.</p>
<p style="text-align:justify;margin-top:12pt;margin-bottom:0pt;text-indent:0%;font-weight:bold;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">Digital &#38; Integration</p>
<p style="text-align:justify;margin-top:6pt;margin-bottom:0pt;text-indent:0%;color:#000000;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">Nine-month 2021 revenue of $2.4 billion increased 7% year-on-year, primarily driven by higher APS project revenue from higher production and improved oil prices, as well as the absence of <span style="color:#000000;">production interruptions in the APS projects in Ecuador that were caused by a major land slide in the second quarter of 2020.</span></p>
<p style="text-align:justify;margin-top:12pt;margin-bottom:0pt;text-indent:0%;color:#000000;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">Year-on-year, pretax operating margin increased 13 percentage points to 34%.&#160;&#160;Operating margin increased due to improved profitability from APS projects as a result of higher oil prices and reduced amortization following the asset impairment charges that were recorded during the first nine months of 2020 relating to certain APS investments in North America and Latin America.</p>
<p style="text-align:justify;margin-top:12pt;margin-bottom:0pt;text-indent:0%;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;">&#160;</p>
<p style="text-align:center;margin-top:12pt;margin-bottom:0pt;text-indent:0%;font-size:10pt;font-family:Times New Roman;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">22</p>
<hr style="page-break-after:always" />
<p style="margin-bottom:0pt;margin-top:0pt;text-indent:0%;font-size:12pt;font-family:Times New Roman;">&#160;</p>
<p style="margin-bottom:0pt;margin-top:0pt;text-indent:0%;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;">&#160;</p>
<p style="text-align:justify;margin-top:18pt;margin-bottom:0pt;text-indent:0%;font-weight:bold;font-size:10pt;font-family:Times New Roman;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">Reservoir Performance</p>
<p style="text-align:justify;margin-top:6pt;margin-bottom:0pt;text-indent:0%;color:#000000;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">Nine-month 2021 revenue of $3.3 billion decreased 24% year-on-year largely reflecting the effects of the OneStim divestiture, which generated $959 million of revenue during the first nine months of 2020.&#160;&#160;Excluding the impact of the OneStim divestiture, revenue declined <span style="color:#000000;">2% year-on-year, largely due to the effects of the pandemic. </span></p>
<p style="text-align:justify;margin-top:12pt;margin-bottom:0pt;text-indent:0%;color:#000000;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">Year-on-year, pretax operating margin increased by 760 bps to 14% despite the significant drop in revenue, primarily due to the divestiture of the OneStim business, which was previously dilutive to margins.</p>
<p style="text-align:justify;margin-top:18pt;margin-bottom:0pt;text-indent:0%;font-weight:bold;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">Well Construction</p>
<p style="text-align:justify;margin-top:6pt;margin-bottom:0pt;text-indent:0%;color:#000000;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">Nine-month 2021 revenue of $6.3 billion decreased 6% year-on-year due to the drop in rig count in North America and internationally due to the effects of the pandemic.</p>
<p style="text-align:justify;margin-top:12pt;margin-bottom:0pt;text-indent:0%;color:#000000;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">Year-on-year, pretax operating margin increased 291 bps to 13% despite the drop in revenue.&#160;&#160;Margin expanded largely as a result of the implementation of cost control measures.</p>
<p style="text-align:justify;margin-top:18pt;margin-bottom:0pt;text-indent:0%;font-weight:bold;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">Production Systems</p>
<p style="text-align:justify;margin-top:6pt;margin-bottom:0pt;text-indent:0%;color:#000000;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">Nine-month 2021 revenue of $4.9 billion decreased 1% year-on-year, primarily driven by the North America short-cycle business due to the significant decline in completions activity as a result of the pandemic.</p>
<p style="text-align:justify;margin-top:12pt;margin-bottom:0pt;text-indent:0%;color:#000000;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">Year-on-year, pretax operating margin increased 25 bps to 10% due to improved profitability in surface and midstream production systems. </p>
<p style="text-align:justify;margin-bottom:0pt;margin-top:18pt;text-indent:0%;font-weight:bold;font-style:italic;font-size:10pt;font-family:Times New Roman;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;"><span style="text-decoration:underline;">Interest and Other Income</span></p>

<p style="text-align:justify;margin-bottom:0pt;margin-top:0pt;text-indent:0%;font-size:12pt;font-family:Times New Roman;">&#160;</p>
<p style="text-align:justify;margin-bottom:0pt;margin-top:0pt;text-indent:0%;font-size:10pt;font-family:Times New Roman;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">The effective tax rate for the third quarter of 2021 was 19%, as compared to 18% for the second quarter of 2021.&#160;&#160;</p>
<p style="text-align:center;margin-top:12pt;margin-bottom:0pt;text-indent:0%;font-size:10pt;font-family:Times New Roman;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">23</p>
<hr style="page-break-after:always" />
<p style="margin-bottom:0pt;margin-top:0pt;text-indent:0%;font-size:12pt;font-family:Times New Roman;">&#160;</p>
<p style="text-align:justify;margin-bottom:0pt;margin-top:12pt;text-indent:0%;font-size:10pt;font-family:Times New Roman;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;"><span style="font-size:10pt;font-family:Times New Roman;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">The effective tax rate for the first </span><span style="font-size:10pt;font-family:Times New Roman;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">nine</span><span style="font-size:10pt;font-family:Times New Roman;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;"> months of 2021 was 19%, as compared to 8% for the same period of 2020.&#160;&#160;The increase in the effective tax rate was primarily due to the charges and credits described in </span><span style="font-size:10pt;font-family:Times New Roman;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">Note 2</span><span style="font-size:10pt;font-family:Times New Roman;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;"> to the </span><span style="font-style:italic;">Consolidated Financial Statements</span><span style="font-style:italic;">.</span><span style="font-size:10pt;font-family:Times New Roman;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;"> </span><span style="font-size:10pt;font-family:Times New Roman;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">These charges and credits</span><span style="font-size:10pt;font-family:Times New Roman;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;"> reduced the effective tax rate for the first </span><span style="font-size:10pt;font-family:Times New Roman;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">nine</span><span style="font-size:10pt;font-family:Times New Roman;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;"> months of 2020 by 1</span><span style="font-size:10pt;font-family:Times New Roman;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">1</span><span style="font-size:10pt;font-family:Times New Roman;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;"> percentage points as a significant portion of these charges were not </span><span style="font-size:10pt;font-family:Times New Roman;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">tax-effective</span><span style="font-size:10pt;font-family:Times New Roman;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">.&#160;&#160;</span></p>
<p style="text-align:justify;margin-bottom:0pt;margin-top:18pt;text-indent:0%;font-weight:bold;font-style:italic;font-size:10pt;font-family:Times New Roman;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;"><span style="text-decoration:underline;">Charges and Credits</span></p>
<p style="text-align:justify;margin-top:6pt;margin-bottom:0pt;text-indent:0%;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">During the third quarter of 2021, a start-up company that Schlumberger previously invested in was acquired.&#160;&#160;As a result of this transaction, Schlumberger&#8217;s ownership interest was converted into shares of a publicly traded company.&#160;&#160;Schlumberger recognized an unrealized pretax gain of $47 million ($36 million after-tax) to increase the carrying value of this investment to its estimated fair value of approximately $55 million.&#160;&#160;This unrealized gain is reflected in <span style="font-style:italic;">Interest &#38; other income</span> in the <span style="font-style:italic;">Consolidated Statement of Income (Loss)</span>.</p>
<p style="text-align:justify;margin-top:12pt;margin-bottom:0pt;text-indent:0%;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">During the first nine months of 2020 Schlumberger recorded the following charges and credits, which are fully described in Note 2 to the <span style="font-style:italic;">Consolidated Financial</span> <span style="font-style:italic;">Statements</span>:&#160;&#160;</p>

<p style="text-align:justify;margin-bottom:0pt;margin-top:6pt;font-size:9pt;font-family:Times New Roman;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;"><span style="font-size:9pt;font-family:Times New Roman;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;"><sup style="font-size:85%;line-height:120%;vertical-align:top">(4)</sup></span></p></td>
<td valign="top">
<p style="text-align:justify;margin-bottom:0pt;margin-top:6pt;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:9pt;">&#8220;Free cash flow&#8221; represents cash flow from operations less capital expenditures, APS investments and multiclient seismic data costs capitalized. Management believes that free cash flow is an important liquidity measure for the company and that it is useful to investors and management as a measure of our ability to generate cash.&#160;&#160;Once business needs and obligations are met, this cash can be used to reinvest in the company for future growth or to return to shareholders through dividend payments or share repurchases.&#160;&#160;Free cash flow does not represent the residual cash flow available for discretionary expenditures.&#160;&#160;Free cash flow is a non-GAAP financial measure that should be considered in addition to, not as a substitute for or superior to, cash flow from operations. </p></td></tr></table></div>
<p style="text-align:justify;margin-bottom:0pt;margin-top:6pt;text-indent:0%;font-size:10pt;font-family:Times New Roman;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">In view of the uncertainty of the depth and extent of the contraction in oil demand due to the COVID-19 pandemic combined with the weaker commodity price environment at the time, in April 2020 Schlumberger announced a 75% reduction to its quarterly cash dividend.&#160;&#160;The revised dividend supports Schlumberger&#8217;s value proposition through a balanced approach of shareholder distributions and organic investment, while providing flexibility to address the uncertain environment.&#160;&#160;This decision reflected the Company&#8217;s focus on its capital stewardship program as well as its commitment to maintain both a strong liquidity position and a strong investment grade credit rating that provides privileged access to the financial markets.</p>

<p style="text-align:justify;margin-bottom:0pt;margin-top:13pt;text-indent:0%;color:#000000;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">Schlumberger maintains an allowance for doubtful accounts in order to record accounts receivable at their net realizable value.&#160; Judgment is involved in recording and making adjustments to this reserve.&#160; Allowances have been recorded for receivables believed to be uncollectible, including amounts for the resolution of potential credit and other collection issues such as disputed invoices.&#160; Adjustments to the allowance may be required in future periods depending on how such potential issues are resolved, or if the financial condition of Schlumberger&#8217;s customers were to deteriorate resulting in an impairment of their ability to make payments.&#160; As a large multinational company with a long history of operating in a cyclical industry, Schlumberger has extensive experience in working with its customers during difficult times to manage its accounts receivable.&#160;</p>
<p style="text-align:justify;margin-bottom:0pt;margin-top:0pt;text-indent:0%;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;">&#160;</p>
<p style="text-align:justify;margin-bottom:0pt;margin-top:0pt;text-indent:0%;color:#000000;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">Schlumberger generates revenue in more than 120 countries.&#160; As of September 30, 2021, only five of those countries individually accounted for greater than 5% of Schlumberger&#8217;s net receivable balance, of which only two (the United States and Mexico) accounted for greater than 10% of such receivables.&#160; </p>
<p style="text-align:justify;margin-bottom:0pt;margin-top:0pt;text-indent:0%;font-size:10pt;">&#160;</p>
<p style="text-align:justify;margin-top:0pt;margin-bottom:0pt;text-indent:0%;font-size:10pt;font-family:Times New Roman;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">At times in recent periods, Schlumberger has experienced delays in payments from its primary customer in Mexico.&#160; Included in <span style="font-style:italic;">Receivables, less allowance for doubtful accounts</span> in the <span style="font-style:italic;">Consolidated Balance Sheet</span> as of September 30, 2021 is approximately $0.7 billion of receivables relating to Mexico.&#160; Schlumberger&#8217;s receivables from its primary customer in Mexico are not in dispute and Schlumberger has not historically had any material write-offs due to uncollectible accounts receivable relating to this customer.</p>

<p style="margin-bottom:0pt;margin-top:18pt;text-indent:0%;font-weight:bold;font-size:10pt;font-family:Times New Roman;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;" id="ITEM_3_QUANTITATIVE_QUALITATIVE_DISCLOSU"><span style="text-decoration:underline;">Item&#160;3. Quantitative and Qualitative Disclosures about Market Risk. </span></p>
<p style="text-align:justify;margin-top:6pt;margin-bottom:0pt;text-indent:0%;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">For quantitative and qualitative disclosures about market risk affecting Schlumberger, see Item&#160;7A, &#8220;Quantitative and Qualitative Disclosures about Market Risk,&#8221; of the Schlumberger Annual Report on Form 10-K for the fiscal year ended December&#160;31, 2020. Schlumberger&#8217;s exposure to market risk has not changed materially since December&#160;31, 2020.&#160;&#160;</p>
<p style="margin-bottom:0pt;margin-top:18pt;text-indent:0%;font-weight:bold;font-size:10pt;font-family:Times New Roman;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;" id="Item_4_Controls_and_Procedures"><span style="text-decoration:underline;">Item&#160;4. Controls and Procedures. </span></p>
<p style="text-align:justify;margin-top:6pt;margin-bottom:0pt;text-indent:0%;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">Schlumberger has carried out an evaluation under the supervision and with the participation of Schlumberger&#8217;s management, including the Chief Executive Officer (&#8220;CEO&#8221;) and the Chief Financial Officer (&#8220;CFO&#8221;), of the effectiveness of Schlumberger&#8217;s &#8220;disclosure controls and procedures&#8221; (as such term is defined in Rules 13a-15(e) and 15d-15(e) under the Securities Exchange Act of 1934 (the &#8220;Exchange Act&#8221;)) as of the end of the period covered by this report. Based on this evaluation, the CEO and the CFO have concluded that, as of the end of the period covered by this report, Schlumberger&#8217;s disclosure controls and procedures were effective to provide reasonable assurance that information required to be disclosed in the reports that Schlumberger files or submits under the Exchange Act is recorded, processed, summarized and reported within the time periods specified in the Securities and Exchange Commission&#8217;s rules and forms. Schlumberger&#8217;s disclosure controls and procedures include controls and procedures designed to ensure that information required to be disclosed in reports filed or submitted under the Exchange Act is accumulated and communicated to its management, including the CEO and the CFO, as appropriate, to allow timely decisions regarding required disclosure. There was no change in Schlumberger&#8217;s internal control over financial reporting during the quarter to which this report relates that has materially affected, or is reasonably likely to materially affect, Schlumberger&#8217;s internal control over financial reporting.</p>
<p style="text-align:center;margin-top:12pt;margin-bottom:0pt;text-indent:0%;font-size:10pt;font-family:Times New Roman;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">28</p>
<hr style="page-break-after:always" />
<p style="margin-bottom:0pt;margin-top:0pt;text-indent:0%;font-size:12pt;font-family:Times New Roman;">&#160;</p>
<p style="text-align:justify;margin-bottom:0pt;margin-top:0pt;text-indent:0%;font-weight:bold;font-size:10pt;font-family:Times New Roman;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;"><span style="text-decoration:underline;">PART II. OTHER INFORMATION </span></p>
<p style="margin-bottom:0pt;margin-top:0pt;text-indent:0%;font-size:6pt;">&#160;</p>
<p style="text-align:justify;margin-bottom:0pt;margin-top:0pt;text-indent:0%;font-weight:bold;font-size:10pt;font-family:Times New Roman;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;" id="Item_1_Legal_Proceedings"><span style="text-decoration:underline;">Item&#160;1. Legal Proceedings. </span></p>
<p style="text-align:justify;margin-bottom:0pt;margin-top:6pt;text-indent:0%;font-size:10pt;font-family:Times New Roman;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">The information with respect to this Item&#160;1 is set forth under Note 9&#8212;<span style="font-style:italic;">Contingencies,</span> in the accompanying <span style="font-style:italic;">Consolidated Financial Statements</span>. </p>
<p style="text-align:justify;margin-bottom:0pt;margin-top:18pt;text-indent:0%;font-weight:bold;font-size:10pt;font-family:Times New Roman;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;" id="Item_1A_Risk_Factors"><span style="text-decoration:underline;">Item&#160;1A. Risk Factors. </span></p>
<p style="text-align:justify;margin-top:6pt;margin-bottom:0pt;text-indent:0%;color:#000000;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;" id="Item_2_Sales_of_Equity">As of the date of this filing, there have been no material changes from the risk factors disclosed in Part 1, Item 1A, of Schlumberger&#8217;s Annual Report on Form 10-K for the fiscal year ended December 31, 2020.</p>
<p style="text-align:justify;margin-bottom:0pt;margin-top:18pt;text-indent:0%;font-weight:bold;font-size:10pt;font-family:Times New Roman;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;" id="ITEM_2_UNREGISTERED_SALES_EQUITY_SECURIT"><span style="text-decoration:underline;">Item&#160;2. Unregistered Sales of Equity Securities and Use of Proceeds. </span></p>
<p style="margin-bottom:0pt;margin-top:6pt;text-indent:0%;font-size:10pt;font-family:Times New Roman;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;"><span style="text-decoration:underline;">Unregistered Sales of Equity Securities </span></p>
<p style="text-align:justify;margin-bottom:0pt;margin-top:6pt;text-indent:0%;color:#000000;font-size:10pt;font-family:Times New Roman;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">None. </p>
<p style="text-align:justify;margin-bottom:0pt;margin-top:18pt;text-indent:0%;font-size:10pt;font-family:Times New Roman;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;"><span style="text-decoration:underline;">Issuer Repurchases of Equity Securities </span></p>
<p style="text-align:justify;margin-top:6pt;margin-bottom:0pt;text-indent:0%;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">As of September 30, 2021, Schlumberger had repurchased $1.0 billion of Schlumberger common stock under its $10 billion share repurchase program. Schlumberger did not repurchase any of its common stock during the first nine months of 2021. </p>
<p style="text-align:justify;margin-bottom:0pt;margin-top:18pt;text-indent:0%;font-weight:bold;font-size:10pt;font-family:Times New Roman;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;" id="Item_3_Defaults_Upon_Senior_Securities"><span style="text-decoration:underline;">Item&#160;3. Defaults Upon Senior Securities. </span></p>
<p style="text-align:justify;margin-bottom:0pt;margin-top:6pt;text-indent:0%;font-size:10pt;font-family:Times New Roman;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">None<span style="font-weight:bold;">. </span></p>
<p style="text-align:justify;margin-bottom:0pt;margin-top:18pt;text-indent:0%;font-weight:bold;font-size:10pt;font-family:Times New Roman;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;" id="Item_4_Mine_Safety_Disclosures"><span style="text-decoration:underline;">Item&#160;4. Mine Safety Disclosures. </span></p>
<p style="text-align:justify;margin-top:6pt;margin-bottom:0pt;text-indent:0%;color:#000000;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">Our mining operations are subject to regulation by the federal Mine Safety and Health Administration under the Federal Mine Safety and Health Act of 1977. Information concerning mine safety violations or other regulatory matters required by section 1503(a) of the Dodd-Frank Wall Street Reform and Consumer Protection Act and Item&#160;104 of Regulation S-K is included in Exhibit 95 to this report.&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;<span style="color:#000000;">&#160;&#160; </span>&#160;&#160;<span style="color:#000000;"> </span></p>
<p style="text-align:justify;margin-top:18pt;margin-bottom:0pt;text-indent:0%;font-weight:bold;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;" id="Item_5_Other_Information"><span style="text-decoration:underline;">Item&#160;5. Other Information. </span></p>
<p style="text-align:justify;margin-top:6pt;margin-bottom:0pt;text-indent:0%;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">In 2013, Schlumberger completed the wind down of its service operations in Iran. Prior to this, certain non-US subsidiaries provided oilfield services to the National Iranian Oil Company and certain of its affiliates (&#8220;NIOC&#8221;).</p>
<p style="text-align:justify;margin-top:12pt;margin-bottom:0pt;text-indent:0%;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">Schlumberger&#8217;s residual transactions or dealings with the government of Iran during the third quarter of 2021 consisted of payments of taxes and other typical governmental charges. Certain non-US subsidiaries of Schlumberger maintain depository accounts at the Dubai branch of Bank Saderat Iran (&#8220;Saderat&#8221;), and at Bank Tejarat (&#8220;Tejarat&#8221;) in Tehran and in Kish for the deposit by NIOC of amounts owed to non-US subsidiaries of Schlumberger for prior services rendered in Iran and for the maintenance of such amounts previously received. One non-US subsidiary also maintained an account at Tejarat for payment of local expenses such as taxes. Schlumberger anticipates that it will discontinue dealings with Saderat and Tejarat following the receipt of all amounts owed to Schlumberger for prior services rendered in Iran.</p>
<p style="text-align:justify;margin-bottom:0pt;margin-top:0pt;text-indent:0%;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;">&#160;</p>
<p style="text-align:center;margin-top:12pt;margin-bottom:0pt;text-indent:0%;font-size:10pt;font-family:Times New Roman;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">29</p>

&lt;td style="background-color:#FFFFFF;padding-left:0pt;padding-Right:0.75pt;padding-Top:0.75pt;width:1%; border-bottom:double 2.5pt transparent;white-space:nowrap;" valign="bottom"&gt;

&lt;td style="background-color:#FFFFFF;padding-left:0pt;padding-Right:0.75pt;padding-Top:0.75pt;padding-Bottom:0pt;width:1%; border-top:solid 0.75pt #000000; border-bottom:double 2.5pt #000000;white-space:nowrap;" valign="bottom"&gt;
&lt;p style="margin-bottom:0pt;margin-top:0pt;margin-left:0pt;;text-indent:0pt;;color:#000000;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;"&gt;$&lt;/p&gt;&lt;/td&gt;
&lt;td style="background-color:#FFFFFF;padding-left:0pt;padding-Right:0.75pt;padding-Top:0.75pt;padding-Bottom:0pt;width:10.94%; border-top:solid 0.75pt #000000; border-bottom:double 2.5pt #000000;white-space:nowrap;" valign="bottom"&gt;
&lt;p style="text-align:right;margin-bottom:0pt;margin-top:0pt;margin-left:0pt;;text-indent:0pt;;color:#000000;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;"&gt;11,539&lt;/p&gt;&lt;/td&gt;
&lt;td style="background-color:#FFFFFF;padding-left:0pt;padding-Right:0.75pt;padding-Top:0.75pt;width:1%; border-bottom:double 2.5pt transparent;white-space:nowrap;" valign="bottom"&gt;
&lt;p style="margin-bottom:0pt;margin-top:0pt;margin-left:0pt;;text-indent:0pt;;color:#000000;font-size:1pt;font-family:Times New Roman;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;"&gt;&#160;&lt;/p&gt;&lt;/td&gt;
&lt;/tr&gt;
&lt;/table&gt;&lt;/div&gt;
&lt;p style="text-align:justify;margin-bottom:0pt;margin-top:0pt;margin-left:6.67%;text-indent:0%;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;"&gt;&#160;&lt;/p&gt;
&lt;p style="text-align:justify;margin-top:0pt;margin-bottom:0pt;text-indent:0%;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;"&gt;&#160;&lt;/p&gt;
&lt;p style="margin-bottom:0pt;margin-top:0pt;text-indent:0%;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;"&gt;&#160;&lt;/p&gt;
&lt;p style="text-align:justify;margin-bottom:0pt;margin-top:0pt;text-indent:0%;font-style:italic;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-weight:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;"&gt;First quarter 2020:&lt;/p&gt;
&lt;p style="text-align:justify;margin-top:0pt;margin-bottom:0pt;text-indent:0%;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;"&gt;&#160;&lt;/p&gt;
&lt;div style="align:left;"&gt;
&lt;table border="0" cellpadding="0" cellspacing="0" style="border-collapse:collapse; width:100%;"&gt;
&lt;tr&gt;
&lt;td style="width:3.33%;white-space:nowrap" valign="top"&gt;
&lt;p style="text-align:justify;margin-bottom:0pt;margin-top:0pt;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;color:#auto;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;letter-spacing:0pt;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;"&gt;&#160;&lt;/p&gt;&lt;/td&gt;
&lt;td style="width:3.33%;white-space:nowrap" valign="top"&gt;
&lt;p style="text-align:justify;margin-bottom:0pt;margin-top:0pt;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;color:#auto;font-size:10pt;font-family:'Times New Roman';text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;letter-spacing:0pt;"&gt;&lt;span style="font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-decoration:none;Background-color:#auto;color:#auto;font-size:10pt;font-family:'Times New Roman';text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;letter-spacing:0pt;"/&gt;&lt;span style="font-size:10pt;font-family:'Times New Roman'"&gt;&#x2022;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/p&gt;&lt;/td&gt;
&lt;td valign="top"&gt;
&lt;p style="text-align:justify;margin-bottom:0pt;margin-top:0pt;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;color:#auto;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;letter-spacing:0pt;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;"&gt;&lt;span style="Background-color:#auto;text-decoration:none;"/&gt;&lt;span style="color:#000000;"&gt;Geopolitical events that increased the supply of low-priced oil to the global market occurred at the same time that demand weakened due to the worldwide effects of the COVID-19 pandemic, leading to a collapse in oil prices during March 2020.&#160;&#160;As a result, Schlumberger&#x2019;s market capitalization deteriorated significantly compared to the end of 2019.&#160;&#160;Schlumberger&#x2019;s stock price reached a low during the first quarter of 2020 not seen since 1995.&#160;&#160;Additionally, the Philadelphia Oil Services Sector index, which is comprised of companies involved in the oil services sector, reached an all-time low.&#160;&#160;As a result of these facts, Schlumberger determined that it was more likely than not that the fair value of certain of its reporting units were less than their carrying value.&#160;&#160;Therefore, Schlumberger performed an interim goodwill impairment test that resulted in a $3.1 billion goodwill impairment charge.&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/p&gt;&lt;/td&gt;&lt;/tr&gt;&lt;/table&gt;&lt;/div&gt;
&lt;p style="text-align:justify;margin-top:12pt;margin-bottom:0pt;margin-left:6.67%;text-indent:0%;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;"&gt;Schlumberger used the income approach to estimate the fair value of its reporting units, but also considered the market approach to validate the results.&#160;&#160;The income approach estimates the fair value by discounting each reporting unit&#x2019;s estimated future cash flows using Schlumberger&#x2019;s estimate of the discount rate, or expected return, that a marketplace participant would have required as of the valuation date.&#160;&#160;The market approach includes the use of comparative multiples to corroborate the discounted cash flow results. The market approach involves significant judgement involved in the selection of the appropriate peer group companies and valuation multiples.&lt;/p&gt;
&lt;p style="text-align:justify;margin-bottom:0pt;margin-top:0pt;margin-left:6.67%;text-indent:0%;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;"&gt;&#160;&lt;/p&gt;
&lt;p style="text-align:justify;margin-top:2pt;margin-bottom:0pt;margin-left:6.67%;text-indent:0%;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;"&gt;Some of the more significant assumptions inherent in the income approach include the estimated future net annual cash flows for each reporting unit and the discount rate.&#160;&#160;Schlumberger selected the assumptions used in the discounted cash flow projections using historical data supplemented by current and anticipated market conditions and estimated growth rates.&#160;&#160;Schlumberger&#x2019;s estimates are based upon assumptions believed to be reasonable.&#160;&#160;However, given the inherent uncertainty in determining the assumptions underlying a discounted cash flow analysis, particularly in the current volatile market, actual results may differ from those used in Schlumberger&#x2019;s valuations which could result in additional impairment charges in the future.&lt;/p&gt;
&lt;p style="text-align:justify;margin-bottom:0pt;margin-top:0pt;margin-left:6.67%;text-indent:0%;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;"&gt;&#160;&lt;/p&gt;
&lt;p style="text-align:justify;margin-top:2pt;margin-bottom:0pt;margin-left:6.67%;text-indent:0%;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;"&gt;The discount rates utilized to value Schlumberger&#x2019;s reporting units were between 12.0% and 13.5%, depending on the risks and uncertainty inherent in the respective reporting unit as well as the size of the reporting unit.&#160;&#160;Assuming all other assumptions and inputs used in each of the respective discounted cash flow analysis were held constant, a 50-basis point increase or decrease in the discount rate assumptions would have changed the fair value of the seven reporting units, on average, by less than 5%.&lt;/p&gt;
&lt;p style="text-align:justify;margin-bottom:0pt;margin-top:0pt;margin-left:6.67%;text-indent:0%;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;"&gt;&#160;&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p style="margin-bottom:0pt;margin-top:0pt;margin-left:0pt;;text-indent:0pt;;color:#000000;font-size:1pt;font-family:Times New Roman;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;"&gt;&#160;&lt;/p&gt;&lt;/td&gt;

&lt;p style="margin-bottom:0pt;margin-top:0pt;text-indent:0%;font-size:12pt;font-family:Times New Roman;"&gt;&#160;&lt;/p&gt;
&lt;p style="text-align:justify;margin-bottom:0pt;margin-top:0pt;text-indent:0%;font-size:10pt;font-family:Times New Roman;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;"&gt;The estimated fair value of Schlumberger&#x2019;s &lt;span style="font-style:italic;"&gt;Long-term Debt, &lt;/span&gt;based on quoted market prices at September 30, 2021 and December 31, 2020, was $15.3 billion and $17.3 billion, respectively.&lt;/p&gt;
&lt;p style="text-align:justify;margin-top:12pt;margin-bottom:0pt;text-indent:0%;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;"&gt;During the second quarter of 2021, Schlumberger replaced its &#x20ac;1.54 billion one-year committed facility with a &#x20ac;750 million &lt;span style="-sec-ix-hidden:F_000770"&gt;three-year&lt;/span&gt; committed revolving credit facility maturing in &lt;span style="-sec-ix-hidden:F_000771"&gt;June 2024&lt;/span&gt;.&#160;&#160;At September 30, 2021 no amounts had been drawn under this facility.&lt;/p&gt;
&lt;p style="text-align:justify;margin-bottom:2pt;margin-top:12pt;text-indent:0%;color:#000000;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;"&gt;In addition to the revolving credit facility described above, at September 30, 2021, Schlumberger had separate committed credit facility agreements aggregating $5.75 billion with commercial banks, all of which was available and unused. &#160;These committed facilities support commercial paper programs in the United States and Europe, of which $2.75 billion matures in February 2023, $2.0 billion matures in February 2025 and $1.0 billion matures in July 2026.&#160;&#160;Interest rates and other terms of borrowing under these lines of credit vary by facility.&lt;/p&gt;
&lt;p style="text-align:justify;margin-bottom:0pt;margin-top:12pt;text-indent:0%;font-size:10pt;font-family:Times New Roman;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;"&gt;There were no borrowings under the commercial paper programs at September 30, 2021.&#160;&#160;Borrowings under the commercial paper programs at December 31, 2020 were $0.4 billion, all of which&#160;was classified in&#160;&lt;span style="font-style:italic;"&gt;Long-term debt&lt;/span&gt; in the &lt;span style="font-style:italic;"&gt;Consolidated Balance &lt;/span&gt;&lt;span style="color:#000000;"&gt;Sheet&lt;/span&gt;.&#160;&#160;&lt;span style="font-size:12pt;"&gt;&#160;&lt;/span&gt;  &lt;/p&gt;
&lt;p style="margin-top:12pt;margin-bottom:0pt;text-indent:0%;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;"&gt;During the second quarter of 2021, Schlumberger repurchased all $665 million of its 3.30% Senior Notes due 2021.&lt;/p&gt;
&lt;p style="text-align:justify;margin-top:12pt;margin-bottom:0pt;text-indent:0%;font-size:10pt;font-family:Times New Roman;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;"&gt;During the first quarter of 2020, Schlumberger issued &#x20ac;400 million of 0.25% Notes due 2027 and &#x20ac;400 million of 0.50% Notes due 2031.&lt;/p&gt;
&lt;p style="text-align:justify;margin-top:12pt;margin-bottom:0pt;text-indent:0%;color:#000000;font-size:10pt;font-family:Times New Roman;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;"&gt;During the second quarter of 2020, Schlumberger issued &#x20ac;1.0 billion of 1.375% Guaranteed Notes due 2026, $900 million of 2.65% Senior Notes due 2030 and &#x20ac;1.0 billion of 2.00% Guaranteed Notes due 2032.&lt;/p&gt;
&lt;p style="text-align:justify;margin-bottom:0pt;margin-top:0pt;text-indent:0%;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;"&gt;&#160;&lt;/p&gt;
&lt;p style="margin-bottom:0pt;margin-top:0pt;text-indent:0%;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;"&gt;&#160;&lt;/p&gt;
&lt;p style="text-align:justify;margin-bottom:0pt;margin-top:0pt;text-indent:0%;color:#000000;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;"&gt;During the second quarter of 2020, Schlumberger repurchased all $600 million of its 4.20% Senior Notes due 2021 and $935 million of its 3.30% Senior Notes due 2021.&#160; Schlumberger paid a premium of approximately $40 million in connection with these repurchases.&#160; This premium was classified in &lt;span style="font-style:italic;"&gt;Impairments &amp;amp; other&lt;/span&gt; in the &lt;span style="font-style:italic;"&gt;Consolidated Statement of Income (Loss)&lt;/span&gt;.&#160; See Note 2 &#x2013; &lt;span style="font-style:italic;"&gt;Charges and Credits&lt;/span&gt;.&lt;span style="color:#000000;"&gt;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/p&gt;
&lt;p style="text-align:justify;margin-bottom:0pt;margin-top:12pt;text-indent:0%;font-size:10pt;font-family:Times New Roman;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;"&gt;During the third quarter of 2020, Schlumberger issued $500 million of 1.40% Senior Notes due 2025 and $350 million of 2.65% Senior Notes due 2030.&lt;span style="font-size:12pt;"&gt;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/p&gt;

    <us-gaap:DerivativeInstrumentsAndHedgingActivitiesDisclosureTextBlock contextRef="C_0000087347_20210101_20210930" id="F_000438">
&lt;p style="text-align:justify;margin-bottom:0pt;margin-top:18pt;text-indent:0%;font-weight:bold;font-size:10pt;font-family:Times New Roman;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;"&gt;8.&#160;&#160; &lt;span style="text-decoration:underline;"&gt;Derivative Instruments and Hedging Activities&lt;/span&gt; &lt;/p&gt;
&lt;p style="text-align:justify;margin-bottom:0pt;margin-top:6pt;text-indent:0%;font-size:10pt;font-family:Times New Roman;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;"&gt;As a multinational company, Schlumberger conducts its business in over 120 countries.&#160;&#160;Schlumberger&#x2019;s functional currency is primarily the US dollar.&#160;&#160;&lt;/p&gt;
&lt;p style="text-align:justify;margin-bottom:0pt;margin-top:12pt;text-indent:0%;font-size:10pt;font-family:Times New Roman;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;"&gt;Schlumberger is exposed to risks on future cash flows to the extent that the local currency is not the functional currency and expenses denominated in local currency are not equal to revenues denominated in local currency.&#160;&#160;Schlumberger uses foreign currency forward contracts to provide a hedge against a portion of these cash flow risks.&#160; These contracts are accounted for as cash flow hedges, with the changes in the fair value of the hedge recorded on the &lt;span style="font-style:italic;"&gt;Consolidated Balance Sheet &lt;/span&gt;and in &lt;span style="font-style:italic;"&gt;Accumulated Other Comprehensive Loss.&#160; &lt;/span&gt;Amounts recorded in&lt;span style="font-style:italic;"&gt; Accumulated Other Comprehensive Loss &lt;/span&gt;are reclassified into earnings in the same period or periods that the hedged item is recognized in earnings.&#160; &lt;/p&gt;
&lt;p style="text-align:justify;margin-bottom:0pt;margin-top:12pt;text-indent:0%;font-size:10pt;font-family:Times New Roman;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;"&gt;Schlumberger is also exposed to risks on future cash flows relating to certain of its fixed rate debt denominated in currencies other than the functional currency.&#160;&#160;Schlumberger uses cross-currency swaps to provide a hedge against these cash flow risks.&#160;&#160;Included in &lt;span style="font-style:italic;"&gt;Other Assets&lt;/span&gt; was $193 million at September 30, 2021 ($427 million at December 31, 2020) and included in &lt;span style="font-style:italic;"&gt;Other Liabilities&lt;/span&gt; was $37 million at September 30, 2021 ($13 million at December 31, 2020) relating to the fair value of outstanding cross-currency swap derivatives.&#160;&#160;The fair value was determined using a model with inputs that are observable in the market or can be derived or corroborated by observable data.&lt;/p&gt;
&lt;p style="text-align:justify;margin-bottom:0pt;margin-top:12pt;text-indent:0%;font-size:10pt;font-family:Times New Roman;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;"&gt;During 2019, a US-dollar functional currency subsidiary of Schlumberger issued &#x20ac;1.5 billion of Euro-denominated debt.&#160;&#160;Schlumberger entered into cross-currency swaps for an aggregate notional amount of &#x20ac;1.5 billion in order to hedge changes in the fair value of its &#x20ac;0.5 billion 0.00% Notes due 2024, &#x20ac;0.5 billion 0.25% Notes due 2027 and &#x20ac;0.5 billion 0.50% Notes due 2031.&#160;&#160;These cross-currency swaps effectively convert the Euro-denominated notes to US-dollar denominated debt with fixed annual interest rates of 2.29%, 2.51% and 2.76%, respectively.&lt;/p&gt;
&lt;p style="text-align:justify;margin-bottom:0pt;margin-top:12pt;text-indent:0%;font-size:10pt;font-family:Times New Roman;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;"&gt;During the first quarter of 2020, a US-dollar functional currency subsidiary of Schlumberger issued &#x20ac;0.8 billion of Euro-denominated debt.&#160;&#160;Schlumberger entered into cross-currency swaps for an aggregate notional amount of &#x20ac;0.8 billion in order to hedge changes in the fair value of its &#x20ac;0.4 billion of 0.25% Notes due 2027 and &#x20ac;0.4 billion of 0.50% Notes due 2031.&#160;&#160;These cross-currency swaps effectively convert the Euro-denominated notes to US-dollar denominated debt with fixed annual interest rates of 1.87% and 2.20%, respectively. &lt;/p&gt;
&lt;p style="text-align:justify;margin-top:12pt;margin-bottom:0pt;text-indent:0%;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;"&gt;During the second quarter of 2020, a US-dollar functional currency subsidiary of Schlumberger issued &#x20ac;2.0 billion of Euro-denominated debt.&#160; Schlumberger entered into cross-currency swaps for an aggregate notional amount of &#x20ac;2.0 billion in order to hedge changes in the fair value of its &#x20ac;1.0 billion of 1.375% Guaranteed Notes due 2026 and &#x20ac;1.0 billion of 2.00% Guaranteed Notes due 2032.&#160; These cross-currency swaps effectively convert the swapped portion of the Euro-denominated notes to US-dollar denominated debt with fixed annual interest rates of 2.77% and 3.49%, respectively.&#160; &lt;/p&gt;
&lt;p style="text-align:justify;margin-bottom:0pt;margin-top:12pt;text-indent:0%;font-size:10pt;font-family:Times New Roman;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;"&gt;During the third quarter of 2020, a Canadian dollar functional currency subsidiary of Schlumberger issued $0.5 billion of US dollar denominated debt.&#160; Schlumberger entered into cross-currency swaps for an aggregate notional amount of $0.5 billion in order to hedge changes in the fair value of its $0.5 billion 1.40% Senior Notes due 2025.&#160; These cross-currency swaps effectively convert the US dollar notes to Canadian dollar denominated debt with a fixed annual interest rate of 1.73%.&lt;span style="font-size:12pt;"&gt;&#160;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/p&gt;
&lt;p style="text-align:justify;margin-top:12pt;margin-bottom:0pt;text-indent:0%;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;"&gt;Schlumberger is exposed to changes in the fair value of assets and liabilities denominated in currencies other than the functional currency.&#160;&#160;While Schlumberger uses foreign currency forward contracts to economically hedge this exposure as it relates to certain currencies, these contracts are not designated as hedges for accounting purposes.&#160;&#160;Instead, the fair value of the contracts is recorded on the &lt;span style="font-style:italic;"&gt;Consolidated Balance Sheet &lt;/span&gt;and changes in the fair value are recognized in the &lt;span style="font-style:italic;"&gt;Consolidated Statement of Income (Loss), &lt;/span&gt;as are changes in the fair value of the hedged item.&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&lt;/p&gt;
&lt;p style="text-align:justify;margin-bottom:0pt;margin-top:12pt;text-indent:0%;font-size:10pt;font-family:Times New Roman;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;"&gt;&lt;span style="font-size:10pt;font-family:Times New Roman;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;"&gt;At&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span style="font-size:10pt;font-family:Times New Roman;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;"&gt; &lt;/span&gt;&lt;span style="font-size:10pt;font-family:Times New Roman;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;"&gt;September&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span style="font-size:10pt;font-family:Times New Roman;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;"&gt; &lt;p style="text-align:justify;margin-top:2pt;margin-bottom:0pt;text-indent:0%;color:#000000;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;"&gt;Due to the actions taken by Schlumberger to reduce its global workforce during 2020, Schlumberger experienced a significant reduction in the expected aggregate years of future service of its employees in its US postretirement medical plan. Accordingly, Schlumberger recorded a curtailment gain of $69 million during the second quarter of 2020 relating to this plan. The curtailment gain includes recognition of the decrease in the benefit obligation as well as a portion of the previously unrecognized prior service credit, reflecting the reduction in expected years of future service.&#160; As a result of the curtailment, Schlumberger performed a remeasurement of the plan, which had an immaterial impact.&#160; This gain was classified in &lt;span style="font-style:italic;"&gt;Impairments &amp;amp; other&lt;/span&gt; in the &lt;span style="font-style:italic;"&gt;Consolidated Statement of Income (Loss)&lt;/span&gt;.&#160; See Note 2 &#x2013; &lt;span style="font-style:italic;"&gt;Charges and Credits&lt;/span&gt;.&lt;/p&gt;</us-gaap:PensionAndOtherPostretirementBenefitsDisclosureTextBlock>

<a href="javascript:void(0);" onclick="top.Show.toggleNext( this );">- Definition</a><div><p>The aggregate costs incurred (1) in a planned search or critical investigation aimed at discovery of new knowledge with the hope that such knowledge will be useful in developing a new product or service, a new process or technique, or in bringing about a significant improvement to an existing product or process; or (2) to translate research findings or other knowledge into a plan or design for a new product or process or for a significant improvement to an existing product or process whether intended for sale or the entity's use, during the reporting period charged to research and development projects, including the costs of developing computer software up to the point in time of achieving technological feasibility, and costs allocated in accounting for a business combination to in-process projects deemed to have no alternative future use.</p></div>
